The CONTROL device formulation incorporates PMACl at 2.0 mg/mL as a passivation additive within the Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85I3 perovskite solution, alongside MACl at 15.0 mg/mL, SAM 4,4,4-NA at 0.5 mg/mL, and PDADI passivation at 0.5 mg/mL. While PMACl partially mitigates interfacial defects, its passivation strength is insufficient to fully suppress non-radiative recombination at grain boundaries and perovskite/SAM interfaces. This limitation manifests in the CONTROL's Voc of 1.18319 V and FF of 81.3931%, indicating unresolved trap-assisted recombination losses that degrade voltage output and charge extraction efficiency. The absence of fluorinated passivators like m-F-PEACl in the CONTROL leaves undercoordinated Pb²⁺ sites inadequately passivated, exacerbating ion migration and interfacial recombination. Replacing PMACl with m-F-PEACl at 2.0 mg/mL leverages the meta-fluoro group's enhanced electron-withdrawing capability, which strengthens binding to defect sites through improved electrostatic interactions. This modification reduces deep-level trap density without altering perovskite stoichiometry, directly addressing voltage losses by minimizing Shockley-Read-Hall recombination. The fluorinated structure also suppresses halide ion migration more effectively than PMACl, stabilizing the perovskite lattice and improving charge carrier lifetime. Although m-F-PEACl may slightly increase solution viscosity, no adverse morphological trade-offs occur due to its structural similarity to PMACl and compatibility with the existing solvent system.

These gains collectively stem from m-F-PEACl's superior defect passivation, which simultaneously mitigates multiple failure modes—grain boundary recombination, interfacial trap states, and ion migration—without compromising film formation kinetics.
